purpose: Global tuning-slider ranges that are the SAME for every car (game-fixed), used to de-normalize sliders the save file stores as 0..1 positions. Unlike data/car-tune-ranges.json (per-chassis), these bands apply to every ordinal.
method: GEAR band shape confirmed on real Data Out telemetry: for the correct band, ladder(mps_per_krpm) x gear-ratio is constant across gears (= tire_radius / final_drive, tire-radius-free). Fitting the 10-speed Honda Beat (ord 3852) gives CV 2.0% at [0.48, 6.00]; Viper ACR / Cayman GT4 / others 4-6% (measurement noise). Absolute scale pinned by physical plausibility (real gear ratios live in ~0.5-5.0; a 2x-scaled band gives absurd 8.8:1 first gears). FINAL DRIVE band from FH tuning calculators, telemetry-consistent. Refine to per-tune EXACT via WheelRotationSpeed: final_drive x gear = CurrentEngineRpm*(2*pi/60) / WheelRotSpeed at a zero-slip frame.

final_drive.source: VERIFIED 2026-09-01 without driving: container Tuning_0412_20260901163403 final_drive position 0.6062 converts through [2.2, 6.1] to 4.56, one of the three final-drive states (4.11 / 4.25 / 4.56) recorded verbatim on the GEARING tab in docs/fh6-ui-spec.md section 3. One point against a band pinned by nine gear points.

gear.source: VERIFIED 2026-09-01 without driving: container Tuning_0412_20260901163403 (9-speed) converted through [0.48, 6.00] reproduces the GEARING tab ratios recorded verbatim in docs/fh6-ui-spec.md section 3 on all 9 gears to 0.01 (4.15 2.75 2.13 1.73 1.47 1.27 1.10 0.93 0.78). Two points pin a linear band; nine agree.

confidence_note: confidence 'derived' = high-quality inference (correct shape, plausible scale), not read-exact off disk. A single WheelRotationSpeed gear-ladder drive on any car upgrades these to verified-exact and can refine the absolute scale. GEAR band upgraded to verified from a screen read paired with its container; a gear-ladder drive is NOT required for gear ratios.

spring_model.formula: k_lb_per_in = freq_hz^2 * W_axle_lb / 19.56 ; W_axle = total_lb * dist(front or rear) ; the slider is linear in spring RATE between the two frequency endpoints
spring_model.formula_source: CONFIRMED against forza.guide's live spring-rate calculator 2026-08-23: at 50/50 it returns front 618.6 / rear 663.6 lb/in for 3086 lb and front 801.7 / rear 860.0 for 4000 lb — both back-solve to a weight-INVARIANT freq (front 2.80 Hz, rear 2.90 Hz), i.e. k = f^2 * W_axle / 19.56 exactly. Also matches the ForzaTune app methodology.
spring_model.recommended_note: forza.guide's RECOMMENDED road spring frequency (a stiff, competitive starting point). Rear ~3.6% stiffer than front. This is a single target point, NOT a slider endpoint.
spring_model.source: Frequency BAND from one observed car whose rate range ratio was 5.00 (=> f_max/f_min = 2.236, e.g. 1.40->3.13 Hz). CORROBORATED 2026-08-23: the recommended 2.80/2.90 Hz sits inside this band near the stiff end, consistent but NOT pinning the endpoints. REFINE: the calculator gives a recommended POINT, not the min/max; the exact endpoints still need one in-game two-point read (a registered spring endpoint + that car's mass).
spring_model.needs: per-car mass+front% in data/car-mass.json (from the My Cars stats capture)
